records.title: PEC-PG 2027: Brazilian government postgraduate exchange programme (master's and doctorate scholarships for students from partner countries)
records.organization: CNPq, CAPES and the Brazilian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Itamaraty)
records.overview: The Programa de Estudantes-Convenio de Pos-Graduacao (PEC-PG) gives graduates from partner countries a monthly stipend (R$ 2,100 for a 24-month master's, R$ 3,100 for a 48-month doctorate) to study at participating Brazilian graduate programmes. For the 2027 round CNPq publishes the list of participating Brazilian institutions in December 2026 and each institution then runs its own selection; scholarships start between March 2027 and March 2028. Applying is free.
records.program_dates: Master's scholarship 24 months, doctorate 48 months; scholarships start between March 2027 and March 2028
records.deadline_text: No single deadline. MRE page (read 21 November 2026): CNPq publishes the final list of eligible Brazilian institutions in 'December 2026', then 'From December 2026 , each HEI/ICT will conduct its own selection of candidates for the PEC-PG program'; scholarships start 'Between March 2027 and March 2028'. Each institution sets its own application dates.
funding_details: MRE page: 'Monthly stipend - R$ 2,100.00 for Master's degree (duration of 24 months) and R$ 3,100.00 for Doctorate degree (duration of 48 months)'
MRE page: access to the Brazilian Public Health System (SUS) 'on the same conditions as Brazilian citizens'
MRE page: financial aid to return to the country of origin, paid by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs 'depending on budgetary and financial availability'

CNPq call notice (PDF, section 5.2.2): PEC-PG does not fund the ticket to Brazil, connections and baggage, lodging of any kind (including installation aid), family allowances, or academic and administrative fees of the Brazilian institution
records.participation_fee: None: the MRE page states 'Application for PEC-PG is free'
records.stipend: R$ 2,100.00 per month for the master's (24 months); R$ 3,100.00 per month for the doctorate (48 months)
eligibility: National of one of the countries participating in PEC-PG and living in one of them (the CAPES list of participating African countries names the Democratic Republic of the Congo)
Completed higher education equivalent to an undergraduate degree (graduacao); no doctorate
No Brazilian nationality (including dual nationality or the right to it) and no permanent residence permit for Brazil
No debts with CAPES or the Brazilian government; able to start within the graduate programme's deadline; an updated Lattes CV
Must also meet the specific requirements of the chosen graduate programme (PPG), including language requirements
nationality_requirements: Nationals of countries participating in PEC-PG who live in one of those countries. The CAPES announcement of the PEC-PG selection (July 2025) lists 29 African participants including 'Republica Democratica do Congo' (the Republic of the Congo is listed separately); the 2027 MRE page refers to 'the countries participating in the Program' without repeating the list.
records.education_requirement: A higher education course equivalent to an undergraduate degree (graduacao); the CNPq call ties its scholarships to academic (stricto sensu) graduate programmes recognised by CAPES
records.language_requirement: Set by each graduate programme (PPG), 'including language requirements'; the research project may be in Portuguese, Spanish or English; the Lattes CV must be in Portuguese
other_requirements: Not already be taking, in Brazil, a course of the same level as the PEC-PG course
Updated Lattes CV on the Lattes platform
Valid ORCID number (listed among the items needed to begin receiving the scholarship)
documents_required: Digital copy of the personal information page of the passport
Proof of CPF (Brazilian taxpayer registry) status
Proof of residence abroad (such as a water or electricity bill)
Research project in Portuguese, Spanish or English
Complete, updated Lattes CV in Portuguese
Statement from the graduate programme confirming regular enrolment (the MRE page lists these to begin receiving the scholarship)
application_process: STEP 1: wait until December 2026, when CNPq publishes the list of Brazilian institutions that may receive PEC-PG students
STEP 2: check which graduate programmes (PPGs) are included and their specific requirements
STEP 3: contact the institutions of interest, or use their websites, to find out how to apply for a PEC-PG scholarship
STEP 4: await the result of the institution's own selection; STEP 5: prepare to travel to Brazil between March 2027 and March 2028

records.title: Universite Senghor (Alexandria): two-year Master en Developpement with living-cost scholarships (Governance and public management, Project management and other specialities)
records.organization: Universite Senghor, direct operator of the Francophonie (Alexandria, Egypt)
records.overview: A professional two-year Master en Developpement taught in French on the Alexandria campus, with eight specialities including Governance and public management and Project management. The 2026 call (21st promotion) offered a living-cost grant to 100 winners of an admission competition open to holders of a Licence with at least one year of relevant professional experience beyond academic internships. The 2026 call is closed; no 2027 call is published yet.
records.program_dates: 2026 call: first year from 20 September 2026; second year from 5 September 2027; end-of-studies internship between 31 January and 16 June 2028; diplomas 18 June to 13 July 2028 (dates indicative, per the 2026 call)
records.deadline_text: No open call. The 2026 call page (read 21 November 2026) shows 'Registration deadline April 1, 2026, 12:00 AM GMT', 'Deadline passed', and says the online file 'doit etre rempli obligatoirement en ligne avant le 15 mars 2026 minuit GMT'. No 2027 call is published.
records.expected_next_cycle: Not announced. Pattern only: the 2026 call opened on 28 January 2026 and closed in March/April 2026, so a similar window in early 2027 is likely but not stated by the organiser.
funding_details: 2026 call: a living-cost grant ('bourse de frais de vie') for 100 winners, who pay only a flat EUR 400 administrative registration fee per year of Master

Living costs covered: individual studio on the campus, one lunch a day, medical insurance, a monthly allowance of 4000 LE per month of effective presence, and a weekend shuttle subject to a minimum number of interested students
Contribution to the end-of-studies internship (return ticket and associated visa fees, travel insurance in 2028); internship allowances are not paid
Not covered: the return trip from the country of residence to Alexandria; a EUR 30 fee is due for the written admission test

records.title: E-JUST TICAD9 African Scholarship for STI, Fall 2027 intake (M.Sc. and Ph.D. at the Egypt-Japan University of Science and Technology)
records.organization: Egypt-Japan University of Science and Technology (E-JUST), with JICA (Japan)
records.overview: Reported by secondary sources (the E-JUST page could not be read): the TICAD9 scholarships for science, technology and innovation (STI) offer 20 M.Sc. and 22 Ph.D. places for the Fall 2027 semester at E-JUST in Egypt, described as a cost-sharing scheme between E-JUST and JICA. The fields listed are Engineering, Computer Science and Information Technology, Basic and Applied Sciences, International Business and Humanities. Applicants are expected to be researchers or instructors, or people potentially expected to become them.
records.program_dates: Reported by secondary sources: Fall 2027 semester; two years for the M.Sc. and three years for the Ph.D., each with six months of preparatory courses if necessary
records.deadline_text: Reported by secondary sources, not confirmed by E-JUST: Opportunities for Africans (12 Nov 2026) states 'Application Deadline: January 10, 2027'; Opportunity Desk (12 Nov 2026) shows 'Deadline: Unspecified'. The E-JUST page could not be read.
funding_details: Reported by secondary sources (E-JUST page not read): 'a fully funded scholarship' covering tuition fees, single accommodation in the E-JUST dormitory, a monthly stipend, medical care and the international round-trip flight from and to the home country; Ph.D. students may receive a research visit to Japan of up to six months, conditional on prerequisites

The flyer for the previous intake (Fall 2025, TICAD8) on the Embassy of Japan in Namibia site lists the same kinds of support under 'Fully Funded Scholarships': tuition fees, flight tickets, accommodation, medical insurance and a monthly stipend
No amounts are given on any page read

Nationality of a country in Africa except Egypt, with a current home address in an African country
Must meet E-JUST's admission requirements and pass the academic interview and oral examination
Applicants who will return to their home university or institution are preferred; the institution's endorsement of the application form is then required
